A LITTLE DIRECTION

Your scene starts here.

Choose a tool and click the canvas to add cameras, lights, talent, or choose items from Walls, Props, Set, and Lights. You can also drag an item directly from the library or toolbar onto the scene map. On a touch screen, hold briefly, then drag; swipe without holding to scroll the library. Release outside the map or press Escape to cancel. Dragging a straight wall sets its start point; choose the endpoint to finish. Room shapes in Walls move as one object; drag their corner handles to resize or enter exact dimensions in Properties. For walls, click a start point and an end point. Drag empty map space to select multiple items. Box select (B) lets you start over an item. Hold Shift to add to a box selection, or Shift-click to add or remove one item. Drag a selected item to move the selection together. Shift-click individual walls, or use Select multiple walls in Properties, then Group selected walls to move and resize them together. Ungroup walls restores individual editing. Doors and windows snap to walls. Open doors and uncovered windows admit light; closed doors and curtains block it.

V Select & move
W Draw a wall
C Add camera
L Add light
A Add talent
Space Drag to pan
⌘ Z Undo
⌘ ⇧ Z Redo
⌘ D Duplicate
⌫ Delete selection
Esc Cancel / deselect
0 Fit scene

Select talent and drag its forward round handle to change facing direction. Select a camera or fixture light and drag its forward round handle to aim. Hold Shift for 15° steps. Its coverage cone or beam updates while you drag.

Drag an image onto the map, or use Bring in a reference. Select it on the map and drag a square handle to resize or the round handle to rotate. Hold Shift at a corner to preserve proportions, or while rotating for 15° steps. Adjust opacity in Properties. Trace walls over a floor plan to create shadows.

Use the Productions selection menu to switch projects, and + to create one. Right-click a scene to delete it. Drag the panel dividers to resize your library and properties. Drag the horizontal divider beneath Scenes to give more space to scenes or items. Search finds items across all four libraries. Select talent, a camera, or a light to record A, move it, and record B. The map shows the route and Preview movement animates it. Play scene beside Undo and Redo previews every recorded route together; Pause freezes the scene and Resume continues it. Scene layers has its own tab beside Properties. Fixtures support color temperature or RGB channels.

Measurements use inches and convert to feet at 12 inches. Enter a size as 8 in, 5 ft 6 in, or a number of inches. Grid dots are 1 foot apart; snapping moves in 1-inch steps. Reference images can be scaled by setting their width to a known real-world dimension.

In Production Desk, open Shot list and choose Export shots. In Scenic, choose Import shot list CSV under Productions. Choose the scenes to import. New scenes get empty maps; matching scene and shot numbers update existing details while preserving your cameras, links, and coverage checks. Shots missing from the CSV stay in Scenic. Place a camera, then choose Link to shot in Properties. Linking applies a supported lens and shot size; every original camera detail stays available below. Use Shot list to see missing camera links and check coverage. Scenic coverage is separate from the original Production Desk shooting status.

Projects autosave on this device. Use Save as… to save an editable .scenic file with every scene and reference image. Choose Share to send a copy to another iPhone, iPad, computer, or collaborator. They can use Import project… to edit their own copy. Import adds a separate production and preserves existing work. Scenic for iOS supports iPhone and iPad. Changes travel in files; send a new copy to exchange further edits. Export map creates a PNG of the scene. Lighting is an artistic 2D approximation, without bounce, height, or calibrated lux.
